depth_justification: It does react to RecoverNow's exact data (photo food logs flagged as biometric, optional weight, free-text meal logs as Art. 9 data) and cites MDR/ISO 82304-2 fittingly for an eating-disorder clinical app, but the identical four-section block (P1.D1, P2.D3, P3.D1, P4.D2) is repeated verbatim five times with zero progression, which dominates the response.
actionability_justification: Although it delivered the requested severity-grouped report, the mitigations stay directional ('obtain explicit consent', 'anonymize/pseudonymize', 'ensure explainability', 'conduct algorithmic impact assessments') with no concrete how — no encryption specifics, no layered-consent design, no retention numbers.
salient_examples: Photos of food may include biometric data ... special category data under GDPR
If the app is considered a medical device ... aligned with ISO 82304-2
The same '1. Data Privacy & Security ... 4. User Autonomy & Informed Consent' block is emitted verbatim five consecutive times
Mitigation: Provide clear, plain-language consent / Use encryption, access controls, and secure cloud storage
